title: Proper sense: lighter sins that do not break charity or earn hell
source_text: III. Denique peccata venialia ex natura & ratione peccati, illis dicuntur peccata leviora, quae, ut ipsi judicant, cum proximi charitate non pugnant, & aeternae poenae reatum non inducunt. Et haec est apud ipsos propria venialis peccati acceptio. Atque hoc sensu sumpta peccata venialia simpliciter & absolute opponi censent peccatis mortalibus; quo nomine designant peccata graviora, quae cum charitate & amore Dei consistere non possunt, & hominem apud Dei tribunal aeternae poenae reum constituunt.
pass_a_gloss: Finally, sins venial from the nature and reason of sin are called by them the lighter sins which, as they judge, do not fight with the charity of neighbor and do not bring in the guilt of eternal punishment. And this is among them the proper acceptation of venial sin. And sins venial taken in this sense they hold to be opposed simply and absolutely to mortal sins; by which name they designate the graver sins which cannot stand with the charity and love of God, and which constitute a person guilty of eternal punishment before God’s tribunal.
pass_b_english: In the proper Roman sense, venial sins are lighter faults that do not war with charity or incur hell’s debt.
Mortals are the graver acts that cannot coexist with love of God and make one liable to eternal punishment.
